items.stem: Which of the following best describes "authoritarian personality"?

items.stem: Outline the findings of Adorno et al. (1950) and explain one conclusion about personality explanations of prejudice that can be drawn from them.

items.stem: "Prejudice is mainly caused by having an authoritarian personality." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Personality explains only some variation; whole societies can show prejudice through norms (Pettigrew, 1958) and group processes, which personality cannot explain.

items.stem: Explain how the authoritarian personality explanation and the conformity explanation would predict different patterns of prejudice in a society.

items.stem: Using Sherif et al. (1961) as supporting evidence, explain competition and cooperation in intergroup relations.
items.answer: Sherif et al. (1961). Aim: to investigate whether competition for resources produces intergroup conflict and whether superordinate goals reduce it. Method: 22 white, middle-class 11-12-year-old boys at a summer camp in Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma (1954) were divided into two groups; after a week of bonding, they competed in a tournament; finally they worked on superordinate goals. Researchers acted as camp staff and observed covertly. Findings: competition produced hostility, name-calling and raids; simple contact did not reduce it, but superordinate goals (fixing the water supply, moving a truck) did Link: competition and cooperation in intergroup relations.
